official.description_text:
Postdoc in AI and digital modelling of electric power systems
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Job description
Do you want to build the models, data and computing environments needed to analyse and control the power system of the future? The Division of Electric Power and Energy Systems is looking for a postdoc in digital modelling and AI for electric power systems. You will work in a research project centred on AI, software development and data modelling of electric power systems, in which a national digital twin of the Swedish power system is being built, with open datasets, catalogues of information models and interfaces, and demonstrators for data exchange between grid companies, flexible customers, aggregators and the electricity market. The work is carried out in close collaboration with industry and grid operators.
The main part of the work consists of developing methods and supporting software for analysis, modelling, optimisation and control of electric power systems from a system perspective. The position includes:
building a development environment with databases and computing platforms for developing and training AI models for power system applications
independently carrying out the tasks for which KTH is responsible in the projects: method and software development, reporting and documentation
publishing the results scientifically and presenting them to the project partners
following developments in the field
Some supervision of students may occur. The work may involve handling data on the Swedish power grid that is subject to protective security legislation.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
The subject area of the doctoral degree must be electric power engineering or a closely related field, with a focus on modelling, machine learning or optimisation at the power system level.
Documented experience of software development for the analysis of large datasets, for example in Python or Julia.
Good command of Swedish and English, spoken and written, as this will be required in day-to-day work.
As a person you are independent, creative and structured, and you collaborate well with colleagues and external partners. We would also like you to be aware of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality.
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
Documented research expertise in the field, evidenced by publications.
Good knowledge of open source solutions in the field, for example pandapower, PowerSystemBlocks, Grid2Op and/or CIM-based tools.
Experience of using and developing data and computing platforms: databases, containerisation, version control and cloud or HPC resources.
Experience of information models and protocols for data exchange in the power system, for example CIM, OpenADR or OCPP.
Experience of collaboration with industry or grid operators in applied research.
Teaching experience, for example supervision of students.
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Maximally two pages long.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The position offered is for, at the most, three years.

ai.summary: Postdoctoral position in AI and digital modelling for electric power systems, building a national digital twin of Sweden's power grid. Work includes ML method development, software engineering, data modelling, and collaboration with grid operators and industry partners.

thematic_fit.rationale: No thematic alignment. The position is domain-specific to power systems engineering and grid optimization. The researcher's domains are human-centred XR, collaborative learning, spatial cognition, and immersive systems. 'Digital twin' appears in both researcher profile and this posting, but context is entirely different—here it refers to infrastructure modelling and optimization; in the researcher's work, it refers to campus spatial representation for learning. No overlap in core themes.

methodological_fit.rationale: Weak methodological fit. Position emphasizes software development (Python/Julia), ML model training, data platforms, and systems integration—all technical. Researcher has intermediate Python (beginner level) and is strong in Unity/C# game engines. The 'software development' overlap is real but divergent in practice (ML infrastructure vs. interactive application development). No user-centred methods, no HCI, no evaluation of user experience. The interdisciplinary collaboration aspect is present but applied to grid operators, not end users or learning outcomes.

growth_value.rationale: Moderate growth value for technical infrastructure skills. Position would deepen Python/ML expertise and expose researcher to large-scale data systems, databases, cloud/HPC platforms, and cross-disciplinary collaboration with industry. However, these capabilities would not directly serve human-centred immersive systems research unless researcher later applies them to XR backend systems (e.g., multiplayer sync, data analytics for user behaviour). Opportunity cost is significant relative to HCI-focused positions.

strategic_value.rationale: Limited strategic value for target identity. Position is at KTH (target geography, Sweden) with strong industry partnerships and funding stability. However, the research domain (power systems) is orthogonal to immersive systems and HCI. Supervisor group (Electric Power and Energy Systems) has no XR/HCI expertise. The applied research context and industry collaboration are valuable, but not in service of the researcher's target trajectory. Risk of career divergence is moderate-to-high.

eligibility_flags: Requires PhD in 'electric power engineering or a closely related field, with a focus on modelling, machine learning or optimisation at the power system level'; researcher's MSc is in creative multimedia, not engineering or energy systems

Requires 'documented experience of software development for the analysis of large datasets, for example in Python or Julia'; researcher has beginner Python, no documented large-scale data engineering projects
Requires 'good command of Swedish and English'; researcher profile indicates English proficiency but no Swedish documented
Position explicitly asks for power systems expertise; researcher has none
risks: Academic background mismatch; no training in power engineering or energy systems—would require substantial ramp-up in domain knowledge
PhD eligibility gate; researcher is MSc by Research (in progress), not PhD—major eligibility blocker
Career pivot risk; postdoc in power systems modelling would further distance researcher from human-centred immersive systems trajectory
Supervisor group (Electric Power and Energy Systems Division) has no connection to HCI, XR, or immersive learning—limited mentorship for maintaining research identity
Industry collaboration is with grid operators, not education, learning, or user experience contexts
